stage1.impression: A moody, backlit misty-wood idea with a believable forest floor and raking shafts of light, and the speaker sits on the ground with a real contact shadow. But the frame is a milky peach wash: the trunks are smooth featureless columns, the 'fire' is glowing cones and dots, there is no readable smoke plume, and the speaker reads as a dull brown box rather than smoked black acrylic. It reads as a competent CG render, not a photograph.

blocking_9: Trunks must show real bark texture and micro-contrast (lum_range on a mid-ground trunk above 70, currently 33).

The smoke must read as woodsmoke: a visible, structured plume rising from the pile with billows and torn edges, grey not peach (plume region lum profile varying by more than 40 between bins, currently 192-217 flat).
The burn pile must look like a real smouldering pile: no cone flames, embers as irregular glowing cracks, not round dots.
The speaker must read as smoked black tinted acrylic with the white lining glowing through, not warm brown (body delta-E to #1A1A1C under 8, currently 13.6).
A grade with real blacks and a neutral-to-cool smoke colour (frame b_median within 30 of r_median, currently 117 vs 175).
Room for type: an area of quiet, even tone that is designed, not just washed-out haze.

defects.what: Mid-ground trunks are smooth grey cylinders with no bark detail; lum_range 33 on the 760-820 trunk.
Left trunks equally textureless, read as fog-wrapped CG columns.
Flames are visibly geometric cones (six 'glowing cones').
Embers are round bokeh-like dots on a soft blob; reads as particles, not a burn pile.
No readable smoke plume above the pile; region is a flat bright wash (lum 192-217).
Global peach/salmon cast; smoke specified grey #A9A6A1 / haze #BCC4CE renders warm (frame r 175, g 142, b 117).
Upper third is a featureless bright haze (lum median 191); depth and the photographed misty wood are lost.
Speaker body reads warm brown (RGB 67,50,41), not smoked black; copper edge glow on all vertical edges looks like an outline/rim from studio lights.
Small disc at the horn's back left edge has a bright, cut-out rim; looks pasted.
Thin bright vertical supports between horn and cabinet catch light unnaturally; read as wire artefacts.
Light shaft on ground has a hard, sharp-sided band that runs straight into camera; looks like a spotlight stripe.

changes.problem: The whole frame is drowned in a uniform peach haze, killing depth, the plume and the photographed wood.

evidence.measured: upper third lum median 191, p5 124; mid trunk lum_range 33; frame r/b medians 175/117

change.setting: Smoke: between the trunks density; uniform haze
change.to: trunk smoke 0.04, uniform haze 0.003, so the plume becomes the dominant smoke mass

changes.expected: Background trunks separate in depth steps; upper third darkens to ~160-175 with visible tree silhouettes and the plume stands out against it.

changes.problem: The plume, the frame's idea ('Where there's smoke'), is invisible.

evidence.measured: vertical profile 205,202,201,217,216,211,209,192: flat, no billow structure

change.from: density 7.0 falling 0.8 per cell, cool fill 12
change.to: density 12 falling 0.6 per cell, cool fill 25 from camera left, and sun-lit side so the billows get light and shadow; keep the lean 2.6 m left

changes.expected: A distinct grey column with lit and shaded billows rising from the pile and leaning left behind the speaker.

changes.problem: The grade is salmon-warm; woodsmoke at dawn should be grey-blue with warmth only in the sun shafts and fire.

change.to: sun #FFD9B4, add a white balance shift of -400 K in the finish, contrast 0.28

changes.expected: Smoke reads neutral grey-blue in shadow, warm only in the shafts; blacks deepen.

changes.problem: The burn pile reads as CG: cone flames and round ember dots.

evidence.measured: visible cone shapes at x 900-960, y 425-470; embers are uniform discs

change.setting: Burn pile: flames and ember chips
change.from: six glowing cones, ember chips emission 90
change.to: remove the cones (a smouldering pile has no tall flames); put emission into a cracked-ember noise texture on the logs' undersides, emission 40, and partly occlude with ash

changes.expected: A low, smouldering orange glow under charred logs feeding the plume; no discrete shapes.

changes.problem: The modelled trunks show no bark; they read as smooth columns.

change.to: pine_bark with displacement 2-3 cm, texture scale so plates are ~8-15 cm, and darker albedo; add two near trunks out of the heaviest smoke so bark reads

changes.expected: Trunks show plated bark with dark fissures; mid-ground trunk contrast at least doubles.

changes.problem: The speaker reads warm brown with copper outlines, not smoked black acrylic; the rim lights look like studio lighting.

change.setting: Speaker lights: fire rim and warm kicker; cool fill
change.to: fire rim 50, kicker 30 #FFC79A, cool fill 6.0, so the black reads with only a thin warm edge on the pile side

changes.expected: Body reads near-neutral smoked black with depth through the tint; warm edge only on the right side facing the pile.

changes.problem: The foreground light shaft is a hard-edged stripe that pulls the eye away from the speaker.

change.from: sun through two shadow-only canopy layers, angle as is
change.to: add sun angular size 1.5 degrees and break the canopy gap that throws this shaft with a branch so the shaft lands across the speaker's feet instead

changes.expected: Ground shafts soften at the edges; the brightest ground patch falls at the speaker's base.

changes.problem: Too little true black anywhere; the image lacks punch for a full page.
changes.expected: Darkest ground and speaker shadows drop to ~25-35, frame gains depth.

out_of_scope.request: Check the thin bright supports between horn and cabinet and the bright-rimmed disc behind the horn; they read as artefacts.
out_of_scope.why: They are parts of the speaker; if they are modelling errors, that is a product-model fix, not a set or light change.
